- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) and news volume is high, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% in subsequent 3–5 periods.  
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (change > -1.00) within 3–5 days, model often lags; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next 2–3 periods.  
- When sentiment is neutral or bearish (≤ 0.00) and news volume is low, model tends to underestimate; add 1–2% upward bias for next 3–5 periods.  
- Model consistently underestimates in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile (change > 0.50 or < -0.50) — apply mean reversion correction: forecast = prior 30d avg + 0.5×(true - prior 30d avg).  
- If sentiment change is negative and news volume is high, model often overreacts; reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 2–4 periods.  
- In cases where model forecast is > 10% above true outcome, check for sentiment reversal or news saturation — apply downward correction proportional to sentiment decay rate.
